entries.definition: extremely evil or cruel; expressive of cruelty or befitting hell
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts design behind the cruelty: intelligence at work, not the blind brutality of *atrocious*.
examples: fires lit up a diabolic scene
diabolical sorcerers under the influence of devils

entries.definition: extremely evil or cruel; expressive of cruelty or befitting hell
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The longer form of *diabolic*, and the extra syllable gives it room to sound theatrical rather than clinical.
examples: diabolical sorcerers under the influence of devils

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The bare verdict: it names the wrongness itself and says nothing of the manner, which is what *atrocious* and *fiendish* are for.

entries.definition: extremely evil or cruel; expressive of cruelty or befitting hell
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most gleeful of these: the cruelty is relished, ingenuity taking pleasure in itself.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and bookish where *atrocious* is loud, delivering the same charge of brutality in a cold register.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Weighs the damage rather than the outrage — gravity where *atrocious* offers shock.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the cruelty outside the human, judging the doer as a kind of creature rather than as someone behaving badly.
examples: no excess was too monstrous for them to commit

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Harsher than *corruptive*, since what it names does not merely degrade a thing but bends it out of true.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes the influence contagious — something to be kept clear of, not just something to disapprove of.

entries.definition: stemming from evil characteristics or forces; wicked or dishonorable
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Adds menace to the wickedness, so that what it names feels still in motion and threatening rather than simply condemned.
examples: the scheme of some sinister intelligence bent on punishing him

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pushes *sudden* past what anyone was braced for, so the speed itself becomes the complaint.
examples: an abrupt change in the weather

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults the transitions as uneven rather than violent — the thing never settles, but nothing in it snaps.

entries.definition: occurring unexpectedly and requiring urgent action
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and functional beside *explosive* — the unexpectedness registers only because it compels urgent action, not because it startles.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts noise into the suddenness, so where *abrupt* merely catches you unready this one goes off.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Grave rather than merely fast: severity is bolted to the speed, so the word reads as a warning.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Harsher than *choppy* on the same broken transitions: the movement snatches, and the word makes it sound ungoverned.

entries.definition: very sudden and in great amount or degree
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Measures how far the change went as well as how fast it came, which is the dimension *sudden* leaves out.
examples: a sharp drop in the stock market

entries.definition: happening without warning or in a short space of time
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain member of the family, covering both arrival without warning and arrival in very little time, and passing no verdict on either.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Purpose read as cold arithmetic - the aim is granted, the warmth withdrawn.
examples: the most calculating and selfish men in the community

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flatter, drier twin of *calculating*, closer to bare goal-directedness and lighter on the accusation.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most final of the hardened set - the toughness reads as settled all the way through, with nothing soft left to reach.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The darkest reading of the same goal-directedness - purpose taken as plotting rather than planning.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal, and the toughness comes with a swagger - the unfeeling is worn rather than lamented.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Chilly rather than cruel - feeling is simply switched off, and nothing is said about what the coolness is for.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain statement of the condition, naming the lost feeling without *hard-boiled*'s relish or *case-hardened*'s finality.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns the same purposefulness as *calculating*, but puts the weight on the plan rather than on the coldness of the planner.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The one word here that credits the goal-directedness, treating aim and judgement as sharpness rather than as a fault.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Not a verdict but a likeness - it measures hardness against metal and leaves the reader to decide whether that is a fault.
examples: steely nerves like those of a steeplejack

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Here the marks stand as proof of what was come through, so the damage reads as standing earned rather than harm suffered.

entries.definition: discolored by coagulation of blood beneath the skin
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names the bruise by its two colours, homely and concrete beside the graver *livid*.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Structural and bloodless: the joint has come apart, and the word says nothing at all about pain.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The exact term for a joint driven out of place, diagnostic where *disjointed* sounds merely come-apart.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most graphic member: the body opened and emptied, damage gone past anything that could still be called a wound.

entries.definition: suffering from physical injury especially that suffered in battle
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The softest word here for real physical injury - it carries the gloss's lean toward battle lightly, and shows nothing of the wound itself.
examples: ambulances … for the hurt men and women

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flat report that harm was done, holding back every picture of it that *mangled* insists on showing.

entries.definition: having edges that are jagged from injury
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The clipped form for flesh left with jagged edges, cool in shape even though the picture it raises is not.

entries.definition: having edges that are jagged from injury
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The ordinary participle for that same ragged tearing, felt rather than measured, where *lacerate* stays curt.

entries.definition: discolored by coagulation of blood beneath the skin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same pooled discoloration in a leaden, grim register that makes the skin sound like something has gone badly wrong beneath it, where *black-and-blue* keeps it almost domestic.

entries.definition: having edges that are jagged from injury
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most violent of these: the jagged edges read as wreckage, the thing ruined rather than merely cut.

entries.definition: having the surface exposed and painful
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Reports pain rather than shape: the covering is gone and what lies under it is left exposed and stinging, unlike the jagged-edge words beside it.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The barest statement of the same parting at the joint — it neither winces nor diagnoses.

entries.definition: having edges that are jagged from injury
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest word for a ragged injured edge — it names the tearing and stops, where *mangled* piles on ruin.

entries.definition: suffering from physical injury especially that suffered in battle
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Graver and more formal than *hurt* for the same injury, dignifying the damage and letting the battlefield sit close without shutting out other harm.

entries.definition: intrusive in a meddling or offensive manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: An everyday word carrying the whole meddling charge, so the disparagement lands quietly where *officious* announces itself.
examples: bustling about self-importantly making an officious nuisance of himself

entries.definition: intrusive in a meddling or offensive manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Turns the offender into a type, dismissing the whole person rather than the one act *meddling* points to.

entries.definition: gradually intrusive without right or permission
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Stresses the slowness of it - the ground is taken a little at a time, so no single step looks like the violation that *invasive* makes it sound.
examples: we moved back from the encroaching tide

entries.definition: intrusive in a meddling or offensive manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flattest of the meddling group - it faults the getting-in-the-way rather than heaping on the contempt that *meddlesome* carries.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain term for the fault: it names the pushing-in itself, without the added charge of trespass that *encroaching* carries or the contempt in *meddlesome*.
examples: she felt her presence there was intrusive
